sections.title: Communication in the Networked Age
sections.description: Communication technologies, including the internet, social media, and countless online applications create the infrastructure and interface through which many of our interactions take place today. This form of networked communication opens new questions about how we establish relationships, engage in public, build a sense of identity, promote social change, or delimit the private domain. The ubiquitous adoption of new technologies has also produced, as a byproduct, new ways of observing the world: many of our interactions now leave a digital trail that, if followed, can help us unravel the determinants and outcomes of human communication in unprecedented ways. This course will give you the theoretical tools to critically analyze the impact that networked technologies have on social life and inform your assessment of current controversies surrounding those technologies.

sections.title: Communication in the Networked Age
sections.description: Communication technologies, including the internet, social media, and rapidly evolving AI tools, create the infrastructure and interface through which many of our interactions take place today. This form of networked communication opens new questions about how we establish relationships, engage in public conversation, seek information, build a sense of identity, or participate in social change. The ubiquitous adoption of new technologies has also produced, as a byproduct, new ways of observing the world: our interactions with other people and with machines (e.g., chatbots, search engines) leave a digital trail that, if followed, can help us unravel the effects of communication in unprecedented ways. This course will give you theoretical tools to critically analyze the impact that networked technologies have on social life and inform your assessment of current controversies and open debates surrounding the social impact of these technologies.
